intent: The supporting sentence under a DialogTitle that describes the dialog's popup to assistive technology.
typical_uses: A sentence stating the consequence of the dialog's action

dont_use_when.situation: The supporting text under a card's title on the page

invariants.text: DialogDescription renders a p in the body type ramp with the muted foreground color.

anti_patterns.dont: Put the dialog's form fields or long content inside DialogDescription
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep it to a short sentence and place fields and long content in DialogContent after the header

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the description's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the description's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dialog.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A description under the title
good.code:
<DialogHeader>
  <DialogTitle>Delete project</DialogTitle>
  <DialogDescription>This permanently deletes the project and its files.</DialogDescription>
</DialogHeader>

bad.title: A form inside the description
bad.why: Everything inside the description becomes the popup's accessible description through `aria-describedby`, announced when the dialog opens, field included.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, DialogDescriptionState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the description's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: DialogDescriptionState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the description's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dialog.module.css, not through this.
